overview: Cardiovascular technologists and technicians help doctors test and treat heart and blood vessel problems. They run EKGs, stress tests and echocardiograms, measure heart chambers, and assist in cardiac catheterization labs. O*NET rates active listening at 3.88 out of 5 for this job and knowledge of customer service at 4.29, since calming patients is part of each test. Most hold an associate degree, 63% in O*NET data, plus a credential. The BLS May 2025 median is $74,310 across 62,960 jobs. The work is indoors, often in hospitals, with exposure to infection.
pay: Cardiovascular technologists earn a median of $74,310, and pay depends a lot on specialty: the lowest 10% earn under $39,000, often EKG technicians, and the top 10% $121,350 or more. Utah has the highest state median at $113,510, 53% above the national figure. Texas has the most jobs, 6,140.

faq.q: How much do cardiovascular technologists make?
faq.a: The BLS May 2025 median is $74,310 a year. The middle half earn between $47,890 and $98,110, with cath lab and echo specialists near the top. Utah, Hawaii ($111,730) and Massachusetts ($105,580) pay the most, while Oklahoma and Mississippi pay the least.

faq.q: How do you become a cardiovascular technologist?
faq.a: Most complete a 2-year associate degree in cardiovascular technology, which 63% hold in O*NET data, while 13% have a post-secondary certificate. There are 4 related programs, including EKG technology and cardiopulmonary technology. Most employers want professional credentials as well.

faq.q: What does a cardiovascular technologist do?
faq.a: They run heart tests such as EKGs, echocardiograms and stress tests, compare measurements to normal ranges and help during heart procedures. In O*NET data the job ranks above 94% of U.S. jobs for working with people. Monitoring and critical thinking are rated 3.75.

faq.q: What jobs are similar to cardiovascular technologist?
faq.a: Radiation Therapists are a 93% match and earn $105,310, 42% more. Respiratory Therapists are a 92% match and earn $82,280, 11% more, according to BLS May 2025 data. Both need an associate degree program and a license, so the switch is fairly short.
